lead_headline: Weekend recap: seven new restaurant leads detected since Friday, including Snarf's Hampden grand opening, Black Rock Coffee drive-thru conversion, and Spitz RiNo launch

restaurant.blurb: Seven opening leads since Friday: Snarf's Sandwiches Hampden (opened 5/19), Black Rock Coffee Hampden (Panera conversion), Spitz Mediterranean RiNo, Sundae ice cream flagship downtown, plus El Pollo Loco Lakewood, Denver Café & Kava Park Hill, Port of Subs Littleton. Two closures: Taco John's Thornton, California Pizza Kitchen Cherry Creek (confirmed summer 2025 shutdown after 25 years).

liquor.blurb: Day 25 of regulatory blackout — Colorado's liquor license apparatus remains in total suspended animation with zero applications processed, zero status updates logged, zero administrative movement since the April 30 cutoff. The database freeze now spans the entire May calendar as the state's regulatory machinery sits in complete paralysis with no official acknowledgment of the outage, no contingency protocols activated, no timeline communicated to licensees whose business expansion plans remain frozen indefinitely. All 12,396 tracked licenses locked in bureaucratic stasis as the invisible application backlog compounds daily behind administrative walls while officials maintain absolute silence on restoration plans or even basic acknowledgment that normal operations have ceased for nearly a full month.

reputation.blurb: One mention yesterday, sustaining the single-digit daily baseline that defines late May — weekly total hits 62 across 11 sources, up 29% from prior week's 48 as momentum continues building toward month-end. Instagram dominates with 25 mentions (40% of weekly volume), Reddit delivers 11, Denver Post contributes 7, Facebook adds 6, X/Twitter rounds out the top five with 4. Google News RSS drives 98% of discovery (61 of 62 mentions). The week-over-week acceleration persists as May tracking nears completion with 212 monthly mentions accumulated, well above typical run rates as pickup velocity holds steady through the final stretch despite the Memorial Day weekend lull.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +2 since Friday (4 new, 2 canceled) as the weekend window delivers modest gains following the single-subscriber trickle on May 24. MTD advances to +23 (+1.0/day average), 90-day net holds at +135. The seven-day window shows net +1 (15 new, 14 canceled), effectively flat as churn matches acquisition velocity in near-perfect equilibrium. Pattern remains unchanged: May's concentrated mid-month surge (May 12-15) generated the bulk of monthly progress, then activity compressed to minimal levels through a sustained drought that persists into Memorial Day weekend. YTD pace of +1.2/day continues outpacing the anemic MTD crawl, underscoring how thoroughly momentum evaporated after the brief May 12-15 spike as daily flow stabilizes at dormant levels.
